scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Deodhani dance originates from the Bodo community of Assam, India.
The term 'Deodhani' means a woman possessed by God, indicating its shamanic roots.
Male shamanic forms exist as 'Deodha-Joki' or 'Deodhai'.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Deodhani is a ritual folk dance associated with the worship of the snake goddess Marei.
It symbolizes spiritual possession and invocation of divine power through shamanic trance.
The dance is performed as a form of worship and spiritual expression.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: In the undivided Darrang district, Deodhani dance is accompanied by songs called Xuknoni, sung by an Ojha, a traditional chorus leader.
In the undivided Kamrup district, the accompaniment includes the Kamrupi Bor-Dhol drum.
Listen for the Kamrupi Bor-Dhol drum.
The music features choral vocal songs led by an Ojha and rhythmic drumming by the Kamrupi Bor-Dhol, creating a ritualistic and martial atmosphere supporting the shamanic dance.

Deodhani is of Bodo-kachari origin.[1] In the group performance, it essentially comprises 3 or 4 women.
